To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a label-free electrochemi luminescent (Ecl) sensor was designed using molecular beacons as recognition probe, and a facile and sensitive method for DNA assay was developed based on ECL emission of surface unpassivated quantum dots (Qds).
a novel label-free electrochemluminescent (ECl) DNA sensor was fabricated based on the molecular beacon with a thiol-modified stem as a recognition element.
the ECL signal inhibition is a facile label-free electrochemical method for ultrasensitive detection of DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, characterization and application of a novel electrochemiluminscent DNA sensor for label-free detection of DNA.
the design and fabrication of a label-free ECL sensor using QDs and DNAzyme to detect DNA at the femtomole level.
the development of a novel electrochemiluminscent (ECL)-based method for DNA detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed label-free method based on QDs ECL emission is a promising application for ultrasensitive and specific detection of target DNA.
this proposed label-free electrochemi-luminescent ( ECL) DNA sensor is a promising application for ultrasensitive detection of DNA.
the proposed method provides a new approach for ultrasensitive detection of DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a molecular beacon with guanine-rich stem is a versatile tool for the development of a label-free DNA sensor by using a QDs-based ELL system.
the molecular beacon was designed as a recognition probe to hybridize with target DNA to form DNAzyme for ECL inhibition.

the ECL sensor is fabricated by a molecular beacon with the G-rich stem as a probe and surface unpassivated QDs co-immobilized AuNPs as the signal transduction system for ultrasensitive label-free DNA detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECL emission can be inhibited by the hybridization of a molecular beacon to the target DNA, and the formed G-quadrupole architecture is responsible for the ECL inhibition.
the ECL signal inhibition is a promising method for ultrasensitive and label-free DNA analysis.
the ECL emission of surface unpassivated QDs could be effectively applied to the development of label-free ECL DNA sensor for the detection of target DNA at low femtomolar level.
